title: Experimental Eval Snapshot — week of 2027-06-21 to 2027-06-27
summary: Short weekly snapshot capturing: microbatch + groupwise 4-bit quant experiments, a lightweight hallucination/regression eval for a new Llama-3 variant, and KV-cache prefetch behaviour on long-context workloads. Early results show a 1.9x token/sec uplift with minimal quality drift on summarization evals at 4-bit groupwise when microbatching is enabled; KV-prefetch reduces tail latency but increases memory pressure for long sequences.
content:
Context and goals:
- Running a fast exploratory sweep to decide whether to promote groupwise 4-bit quant (G4-q) for onboarded open models used in hosted tiers. Focus: quality regressions (hallucination, instruction-following), latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, and operational risks (OOMs, increased GC).
- Secondary: test KV-cache prefetch + microbatching across 1–8 concurrent sessions to understand tail behavior for chat workloads with long histories.

What we ran (high level):
1) Quantization sweep (G4-q vs 8-bit dynamic)
   - Models: llama-3-8b, alpaca-7b-merged (onboarding candidate)
   - Tooling: qbench v0.12 with streaming sim harness.
   - Configs: microbatch sizes [1,4,8], seq-len evals [512,1024,2048], beam=1 streaming.
2) Hallucination/regression evals
   - Datasets: 200 summarization prompts (NewsSumm-small), 150 instruction-follow prompts (internal instr-50 + community edge-cases).
   - Metrics: ROUGE-L, pass-rate for safety-filter triggers, hallucination-score (manual span-level annotation, coarse).
3) KV-cache prefetch tests
   - Synthetic chat workloads with 6-turn histories, token growth patterns to 1800 tokens.
   - Measured p99 inference latency and resident GPU memory over time.

Key results (numbers are median across 3 runs unless noted):
- Throughput (tokens/sec) on llama-3-8b:
   - FP16 baseline, microbatch=1: 1340 t/s
   - G4-q, microbatch=1: 1120 t/s (0.83x vs FP16)
   - G4-q + microbatch=4: 2490 t/s (1.86x vs FP16)
   - 8-bit dynamic + microbatch=4: 2150 t/s (1.6x)
- Latency (p95 single-request) on alpaca-7b-merged, seq=1024:
   - FP16 microbatch=1: 220ms p95
   - G4-q microbatch=1: 240ms p95 (slight increase)
   - G4-q microbatch=4 (with batching window 10ms): 170ms p95 (batching helps p95 in steady load)
- Quality (summarization ROUGE-L, higher better):
   - FP16: 32.8
   - 8-bit dyn: 32.1 (delta -0.7)
   - G4-q: 31.6 (delta -1.2) — degradation concentrated in numeric accuracy and rare proper nouns
- Hallucination manual pass-rate (lower is worse):
   - FP16: 6/200 flagged
   - G4-q: 10/200 flagged (concentrated in long-context cross-references)

KV-cache prefetch notes:
- Prefetch enabled reduces p99 by ~18% for 6-turn chats at sequence length >1500 tokens, but resident GPU memory increases by ~1.4x because prefetch allocates additional KV pages.
- Observed two OOMs on llama-3-8b + G4-q when microbatch=8 and prefetch was enabled on a 40-concurrency endpoint. Root cause: per-request prefetched KV buffers were not properly reclaimed under stress.
- Mitigation: add soft limit for prefetch pages per endpoint and ensure zero-copy release path (follow-up work below).

Op/regressions and risk items:
- G4-q shows measurable quality drift in numerics and entity-name resolution on cross-doc references; needs targeted evals focusing on citations and numeric prompts.
- Memory OOMs under prefetch+large-microbatch combos need guardrails before we enable in Dedicated customers.
- Observability: current tracer lacks token-level mismatch tracking for quantized paths; alerts don't surface small but consistent delta in ROUGE/QA metrics across releases.

Experiment logs (quick capture):
- run-2027-06-24-q1: llama-3-8b G4-q microbatch=4 seq=1024 — throughput 2480 t/s, ROUGE-L 31.7, p99 210ms
- run-2027-06-25-kv1: alpaca-7b prefetch=on microbatch=4 concurrency=16 — p99 reduced by 15%, memory +35%
- run-2027-06-26-edgecase: llama-3-8b G4-q numeric-checks dataset — failure rate 4% (vs 1% baseline)

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Is the numeric/entity drift systematic across groupwise quantization (group size dependence), or dataset-specific? Next: sweep group sizes [16,32,64] on the failing subset.
- Can we reclaim prefetched KV pages more aggressively without increasing p99? Hypothesis: LRU-style eviction keyed on active session will keep hot sessions fast and reclaim for cold ones.
- Microbatching window tuning: is 10ms optimal? We observed some user-visible latency spikes correlated with batching windows during low load. Consider adaptive window (based on request arrival rate).

To-do / next steps (owner in parentheses):
- Run focused group-size sweep for G4 (16/32/64) on numeric/entity-sensitive prompt set (Riley). Target date: 2027-07-05.
- Add telemetry for token-level quality diffs on quant paths (instrument qbench to emit diffs + aggregate) (Noah). Target: 2027-07-08.
- Implement soft-limit and LRU eviction prototype for KV-prefetch (Zoe + infra) and run 48-hr soak (target: 2027-07-15).
- Draft a short runbook for Dedicated onboarding teams warning about prefetch + large microbatch combos (Asha). Complete by 2027-07-01.

Notes from standup calls this week (abridged):
- 2027-06-23 sync: consensus to deprioritize promoting G4-q to hosted until group-size sweep completes and numerical regressions are mitigated.
- 2027-06-25 triage: OOM root cause identified and repro steps captured in ML-EVAL-219.

Small ideas / experiments to try (brainstorm):
- Hybrid path: keep first N layers at fp16 and last M layers quantized (heuristic: top 8 layers FP16) to preserve numerics while still saving memory.
- Dynamic group-size per-layer based on activation variance (auto-tune during warmup).
- Use a light-weight classifier to route numeric-sensitive prompts to FP16 instances automatically.

Appendix (quick artifacts):
- Microbench commands used (qbench): qbench --model llama-3-8b --quant groupwise-4 --microbatch 4 --seq-len 1024 --stream-sim 1
- Short link to failing prompt examples: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AM/quant-failure-examples

Comments / notes to self:
- Keep this snapshot short and heavy on actionable next steps. Save longer artifacts into the eval run logs.
- If we get group-size=16 results close to FP16, schedule a canary with telemetry for the hosted tier.
